rowKinds.COLLECTION: The existence and count of elements in a collection. Items on a COLLECTION row say that elements matching a selector exist (EXISTS), how many (COUNT/RANGE), or that none may (NOT_EXISTS).
rowKinds.FIELD: An atomic property of one element, or of the game for non-collection rows.
rowKinds.VIEW: Computed from other rows, never stored. Items may constrain a view (checked in Gate B forward); a view never needs support and supports no stored row. Every contract still declares it.

selectorSyntax.note: Added 20 September. The selector language existed only in the grammar sheet prose (RC-11), so nothing in data said how to parse one - and three independent readers validating the same items produced three different failure counts because of it. Extracted here: form changed, language unchanged.
selectorSyntax.attributeNames: An attribute name is taken WHOLE, including dots. V7 registers condition.type and condition.referents as attribute names, so a parser that splits on the dot and validates against condition is wrong - that alone moved one recount from 5 failures to 11.
selectorSyntax.noAttribute: A selector of * or an absent selector uses no attribute and is validated against nothing. Whether such an item counts in a failure tally is a reporting convention, not a rule; state the convention with any count.
selectorSyntax.unregistered: An attribute not in the row selectorAttributes (resolved via ownerRow for a FIELD row) makes the selector unnormalisable: a reference defect under SD-32, never a prose match.

ownerRowNote: Added 20 September. A selector on a FIELD or VIEW row selects the ELEMENT OF ITS OWNING COLLECTION, so its attributes come from that collection selectorAttributes, not from the field row. The register recorded no owner, and the two readings differ across the corpus. RECOUNTED 20 September, three times independently, because three readers produced three different pairs: validating against the owning collection refuses 5 items, and validating against the field row own attributes refuses 59 to 70 depending on whether an item with no attribute in its selector is counted. The load-bearing number is the 5: they are exactly the From Goal Kicks restart=GOAL_KICK items already recorded as a defect, so the ownerRow reading adds NO new failures, while the other reading condemns about 60 items that are sound. ownerRow is now explicit so no implementer has to infer it. A row with no ownerRow is game-level: E1-E4, S1, SV1, P5, P6a, P6b, P7, DV1, V1, V2.
fillableIsExhaustive: A free choice (REALIZATION) is possible only on rows with a 'fillable' entry, and only as that entry says. sourceKinds is descriptive and licenses nothing. SUPERSEDED 21 September: P-4 is no longer the authority. SD-39 is - OPEN is an explicitly authorized degree of freedom within an already-supported property, not a synonym for unknown. These twelve entries survive as DATA: the register statement of which rows have a structurally defined choice space. A fillable entry states the space; it does not by itself authorize a choice, and silence never creates one.

rows.targetOfValues: ADDED 15 October 2026 (register version 10) for his M1 in the reply filed 17 October 2026: "Allow target configurations to reflect each team's role during the block." A region carries targetOf=T where a PRIMARY_SCORING objective (J4) whose team (J3) is T references it (J2). It is the relation the possession game's own region phrase already uses ("of the team J3 names for the objective referencing it"), made selectable, and it is the one term for 'the target a team attacks' (his M8's typed referent reads the same J2/J3 relation). T is a team designation (teamDesignations.designationAttributes): a setup assignment (TEAM_AT_AXIS_*) is met by the region its objective references and not met by the region another setup assignment's objective references; ROLE_HOLDER_<role> is met through the role block the game is derived for, and is undetermined where the game is derived for none. DERIVED, never authored on a region and never written into its selector: the engine computes it before reach from the J1/J2/J3 items (back/src/system/derivation/target-of.ts, answered by designation.ts targetDesignations; the rows are named in the targetOf block below) and nothing else, so a targetOf selector identifies an existing objective region and never creates one (AM-13 preserved; a third region would break ruling C42's 'exactly two active objectives and two corresponding target regions, not three'). Our engineering; his words are the two quoted.
rows.lateralValues: closed list (draft, AM-17), each with its interval test against the element's position.across, on an envelope of width W with the midline at W/2. wide-left: touches the 0 touchline and does not contain the midline. wide-right: touches the W touchline and does not contain the midline. wide: either of those. central: THE SAME TEST AS relativeTerms.central, which is canonical - contains the axis midline across the width, and touches neither touchline. full-width: touches both touchlines. lateral is SET-VALUED: an element carries every value whose test it satisfies, so a wide-left region also carries wide. Intervals are closed at both ends, and touches means shares an endpoint with the touchline. The list is NOT exhaustive - an element touching one touchline and containing the midline (0-20 on W=30) satisfies none, carries no lateral value, and no lateral selector can reach it. An element matching none carries no lateral value. A lateral selector identifies an existing region; it never creates one (AM-13 preserved). These five values are a capability offered to CONTRACT AUTHORS: derivation never rewrites an authored selector or scope to use them (AM-12), so an existing contract gains nothing from AM-17 until it is restated
rows.fillable: element count above an authored COUNT/RANGE minimum and inside its maximum
rows.longitudinalValues: closed list (draft, C42), the along-axis mirror of lateralValues, each with its interval test against the element position.along, on an envelope of length L with the midpoint at L/2. end-near: touches the 0 end line and does not touch the L end line. end-far: touches the L end line and does not touch the 0 end line. end: either of those. longitudinal is SET-VALUED on the same terms as lateral, so an end-near region also carries end. Intervals are closed at both ends, and touches means shares an endpoint with the end line. The list is NOT exhaustive and is deliberately smaller than lateralValues: only the two ends and their union are defined, because the only thing it was authored to do is tell two opposing target regions apart. An element matching none carries no longitudinal value, and no longitudinal selector can reach it. A longitudinal selector identifies an existing region; it never creates one (AM-13 preserved). As with AM-17, these values are a capability offered to CONTRACT AUTHORS: derivation never rewrites an authored selector or scope to use them (AM-12), so an existing contract gains nothing from this until it is restated. NARROWED 15 October 2026 (register version 13, S2.longitudinalValues version 2) on his reply filed 17 October 2026, M7: "M7 — Target relative to pressure reference: Approved if required. The progression target should be permitted at or before halfway when justified by the learning problem. Do not introduce a universal halfway restriction." and D3: "The progression target may be at or before halfway when that better represents successfully playing beyond the initial pressure. Halfway is not a required location." Until then each test also read 'and does not contain the midpoint': no code enforced it (measured by the design verification of 17 October: a target [20,40] passed every gate), and on the register's own definition it would have left a target that begins at or before halfway with no end value, so no longitudinal selector could reach it. That two opposed targets do not overlap - the only work the midpoint clause did - is now GA-DIRECTION's clause 'the opposed objectives' targets do not overlap along the axis', added in the same version.

rows.fillableAuthority: SD-39 (ruled 21 September), the authority for OPEN. It applies to this row only because SD-39's own qualification is met independently: "the property's existence and legitimate choice space must already be supported". The Sport Profile's bounds-only contribution of 6 October supplies exactly that -- it establishes the possession relationship as legitimate game structure over the participating opposing teams and leaves its initial holder unfixed, so the freedom sits inside a supported property rather than standing in for absent knowledge. comparison.relation: NARROWS. Never written with EXCLUSION strictness: a comparative is a relationship, not a prohibition [C20]. It never entails a value and never entails existence
comparison.whereItLands: SD-26. A comparison takes NO LINE. It is a relationship assertion evaluated over its operands, held in the contribution and reconciliation record, outside the eight stored areas. It never takes a property's verdict and never changes a line's status. This replaces the earlier reachesLine rule, which Christian overruled
comparison.boundary: Both operands must be properties the resolved game contains and can evaluate. Never an inferred player state or ecological outcome: not pressure, opportunity, affordance availability, difficulty or uncertainty
comparison.evaluability: SD-26. A comparison is evaluable only when both operands resolve - to a value the game holds and supports, or to a derived quantity whose inputs it holds and supports. Otherwise it is unmet (required) or not evaluable (supporting), by its requirement status. Never quietly true
comparison.relationshipConflict: SD-26. Two comparative requirements that no single assignment satisfies produce an UNRESOLVED RELATIONSHIP CONFLICT - a report of its own kind, not a line status and not a Game status. Raised only when both are authoritative (authored or owner-ruled, never assumed, never engine-only), both well-formed under SD-23, and both evaluable. Fail any of those and it is a gap, a diagnostic tension, or an unmet item instead
comparison.assumedCannotCollide: SD-27. An assumed item may not create an authoritative collision with authored knowledge. Assumed-vs-authored is reported diagnostically as a POSSIBLE TENSION, which no gate reads; it can never drive UNRESOLVED. An interpretation consistent with an object's prose is not promoted to canonical meaning
comparison.gapBeforeCollision: SD-28. A collision requires well-formed, support-capable authoritative claims with sufficiently resolved operands. An unauthored or incomputable dependency is a GAP first, and nothing downstream converts it into a disagreement. An invented or assumed comparative cannot manufacture an authoritative collision
comparison.effectiveValue: SD-24, provisional, in his words: the primary-event base value after application of all applicable resolved value modifiers for the referent. A value modifier must explicitly declare its operation or type (row V9a); multiplier versus increment is never inferred. If an operation or magnitude required for the derivation is unauthored, effective value is NOT COMPUTABLE
comparison.notAnExclusion: A comparative claim is not translated into a mutual exclusion. 'Wide has greater task value than central' is a relationship; it is not 'central value is forbidden' [C20]
comparison.stillOpen: No aggregate function is named (each, some, the sum, the greatest) for a comparison ranging over several matched elements. An engine refuses such a comparison rather than choosing one

FROM_THE_FEET.note: OUR operational gloss, for his sight: the player taking the restart plays the ball from their feet; the ball may be still when play restarts, or the player may receive it and play on. It is NOT IN_HAND, it does not decide who delivers a ball the player receives (a teammate, the coach or either - not settled), and it is not a universal start: an item states it for one activity, and nothing makes a restart begin this way unless an item says so. SD-13 (a stationary-ball or kickoff START) does not fire on it. Added 15 October 2026 (T5.method version 2).
FROM_THE_FEET.basisEvidence: Christian, reply filed 17 October 2026, D5: "The initial demonstration may use goalkeeper distribution from the feet." and "The goalkeeper may receive and play from the feet; a stationary-ball restart should not be universally required." M3: "Support goalkeeper or controlled defensive starts, coach-selected restart locations, and activity-specific restart methods. These choices must remain distinguishable from universal requirements."

contractEnums.declarationQualifierNote: ADDED 15 October 2026 (register version 8) on Christian's M6, approved in his reply filed 17 October 2026. HIS WORDS: "M6 — Explicit no-further-value status: Approved with a safeguard. I approve the narrow authority exception where the added statement provably cannot contradict existing knowledge. However, the machine-readable representation must preserve the distinction between: No further value is required. The value is explicitly unrestricted. A necessary value is missing. These must not collapse into the same operational meaning, even if their current surface representation is similar." OUR OPERATIONAL GLOSSES (engineering, not his words): a qualifier is valid only on a NON_CLAIMED declaration and says which state that non-claim is. NO_FURTHER_VALUE = an explicit statement that the field needs nothing more: an established absence, never filled, nothing said to the coach, and - unlike a legacy non-claim - able to set a ruled deferral aside. UNRESTRICTED = registered so the state exists and stays distinct, but REFUSED AT LOAD until he rules what 'any value' permits on a row; refusing is our fail-closed default, and SD-39 (a non-claim permits a choice only inside an already-supported choice space) is the existing ruled grounding for the alternative reading. Absent = a LEGACY non-claim, 'this object does not constrain this row' (our restater's doesNotConstrain), unchanged; no existing declaration is requalified. A necessary value MISSING is not a qualifier: it stays NOT_AUTHORED or an unresolved CLAIMED, the two that block.

FIRST_FORWARD_PASS.note: An EVENT IN PLAY, like POSSESSION_CHANGE, never a restart like START. Forward is relative to the passing team attacking direction, which the representation establishes (SD-95); where that direction is FREE the trigger is NOT EVALUABLE and its line is CONDITIONAL, never failed. First is per episode, using the episode boundary transitions already carry (startsEpisode). It implies NOTHING about pass success, receiver, distance or intent, and must not be read as doing so. Added 2026-09-29 on Christian ruling; bounded addition only, no qualifier capability is implied.
FIRST_FORWARD_PASS.typedOn: Christian, 2026-10-04: "Please implement the machine-readable evaluability dependency you proposed for trigger semantics and have the admitting check consult it. I do not consider that an architectural expansion. It makes an already-authored semantic dependency enforceable rather than leaving it in prose." The prose above is unchanged and remains the authored reading; evaluabilityDependsOn names the row it already cites. DV1 is `direction`, which holds the attacking direction per team - the thing the note says "forward" is relative to and that the representation establishes (SD-95). Where DV1 is not established, a trigger naming this kind is NOT EVALUABLE rather than admitted on vocabulary membership, which is what the note asked for and nothing enforced.

COMPLETED_PASS.note: An EVENT IN PLAY, like POSSESSION_CHANGE, never a restart like START. COMPLETION IS CONSTITUTIVE AND IS THE WHOLE OF IT: a pass that connects, reaching a player of the passing team. It implies NOTHING about region, direction, receiver identity, distance, intent, control quality, possession, possession change, scoring eligibility, transition or episode boundary, and must not be read as doing so. Whether a pass connected is a judgement made in play; the representation names the kind of occurrence and does not record occurrences. Added 2026-10-04 on Christian ruling; bounded addition only, no qualifier capability is implied.
COMPLETED_PASS.independentOf: NOT a generalization of FIRST_FORWARD_PASS and not its specialization either - the two are INDEPENDENT kinds, on his explicit instruction. FIRST_FORWARD_PASS’s own entry says it "implies NOTHING about pass success", so a forward pass need not connect: an intercepted forward pass is a FIRST_FORWARD_PASS and is not a COMPLETED_PASS, and a completed square pass is the reverse. The trigger vocabulary is therefore not a hierarchy, and no ordering between these two members may be inferred.
COMPLETED_PASS.basisEvidence: Christian, 2026-09-29, the ruling that requires it: "The current connected-pass count is revealed immediately following each qualifying pass and updates progressively as the count changes." What "qualifying" means is fixed by PCG-05 (AUTHORED, REQUIRED, REQUIRED_RANGE): "counts ATTACKING_TEAM’s connected passes; the count resets on {POSSESSION_CHANGE, OUT_END_LINE, OUT_TOUCHLINE}". So the kind is a pass that CONNECTS, and nothing further. PCG-14.b (V19 = IMMEDIATE_AFTER_TRIGGER, OWNER_RULING) is what makes V17 load-bearing by construction: "immediately after the trigger" denotes nothing unless a trigger is named.
COMPLETED_PASS.whyNoDependency: Unlike FIRST_FORWARD_PASS, which depends on DV1 because "forward" is measured against an attacking direction the representation establishes, completion is measured against nothing the representation holds - whether a pass reached a teammate is an in-play judgement. So this kind registers NO row dependency, and a check has nothing to consult for it. Note the consequence, reported rather than repaired: constructTriggers never reads vocabularies.trigger, so a new token is never structurally reachable, and GA-INFORMATION does not test reachability on V17 the way GA-EFFECT-TYPED does on V12. An item authoring this token on V17 is therefore admitted on registration alone and is never asked whether the occurrence can arise.

COACH_JUDGED_EPISODE_CONCLUSION.note: An EVENT the coach judges, in play or at a stoppage: that the meaningful attacking opportunity of an episode has ended. It implies NOTHING about time, possession, a change of possession, a pass or a pass count, a region, the ball going out or a score, and must not be read as doing so. Its episode is HIS (D5): the one a transition beginning a build-out episode begins, which a score or this judgement concludes, and which may span changes of possession - not SD-14's attacking episode (T7) and not SD-36's BUILD_OUT_EPISODE scope, though a transition keyed on it may begin an episode of both kinds. That a judgement made at a stoppage takes the place of that stoppage's ordinary restart is OUR operational reading of his D5 and of his 18 October item 2 ("At any stoppage, the coach may instead conclude the current episode and initiate another build-out."), labelled so. Whether play stops when the coach judges, and how it restarts, is stated by the transition keyed on it (T6-T7), never by this entry. Added 15 October 2026 (trigger version 4) on his M4; the wording of this note is ours.
COACH_JUDGED_EPISODE_CONCLUSION.basisEvidence: Christian, reply filed 17 October 2026, M4: "M4 — Coach-judged episode conclusion: Approved." "Support one explicit coach-judged event representing the conclusion of a meaningful episode." "Do not substitute a timer, possession change, or arbitrary pass count." D5: "An episode concludes when either team scores or when the coach judges that the meaningful attacking opportunity has ended." "The coach may make that judgment at a stoppage or during play." His reply filed 18 October 2026, item 2: "At any stoppage, the coach may instead conclude the current episode and initiate another build-out."
COACH_JUDGED_EPISODE_CONCLUSION.independentOfNote: The substitutes his M4 forbids ("a timer, possession change, or arbitrary pass count") and the occurrences his D5 sets beside it ("when either team scores or when the coach judges"): the judgement is none of them and is not derived from any of them. Not a hierarchy: no ordering between this member and any other may be inferred.
COACH_JUDGED_EPISODE_CONCLUSION.whyNoDependency: The judgement is the coach's, made in play or at a stoppage, and is measured against nothing the representation holds, so no row's establishment is consulted for it (as COMPLETED_PASS).
COACH_JUDGED_EPISODE_CONCLUSION.structuralPrerequisiteNote: OUR operational proposal, labelled so and not his words: SD-44 makes a trigger exist by construction only where its structural prerequisites are in the game, and a conclusion needs an episode to conclude, which begins with a start - so the trigger is reachable where the game holds a transition element keyed on START (engine.ts constructTriggers reads this entry generically; no trigger is named in code). It is a class-level fact, because triggers are constructed before any line is derived. It refers to no pressure, likelihood or play state.

nounSemantics.note: Added 1 October on Christian’s ruling. A noun states the element’s DIMENSIONALITY and nothing about orientation: "zero extent in its thickness dimension and extent in its length dimension", with which axis is which following from the element’s own orientation. Deliberately general - the same noun must describe a line across the playing area and one along it, so no entry here may name an axis.
nounSemantics.oneDimensionalRule: For a noun with extentDimensions 1, the element has extent on exactly one axis. Whichever axis carries its extent is its LENGTH; its extent on the other axis is ZERO. Orientation is therefore read off the geometry already established and is never inferred from the noun.

applicability.note: Added 20 September. Some FIELD rows do not apply to every element of their collection, and the register stated that ONLY inside valueType prose. Without this as data, line enumeration creates lines no author can ever close and Gate A can never pass. A row listed here yields NO line for an element whose condition fails; it is not NOT_AUTHORED, it is not applicable.
applicability.grammar: Each entry is { when: { row, sameElement, in: [values] }, text }. The condition reads the GOVERNING line for the same element (a transition, or a consequence). Evaluated at stage 6, after the governing line is resolved.
applicability.governingLineRule: If the governing line is DERIVED, the condition is evaluated: true keeps the dependent line, false WITHDRAWS it (not applicable, never NOT_AUTHORED). If the governing line is FREE(choice), the dependent line is CONDITIONAL on that choice: it takes no value, is not open in its own right, and a gate check over it is a satisfiability question across the governing choice. If the governing line is FAILED, the dependent line is FAILED as a GAP whose dependency is the governing line - gap before collision, and never withdrawn, because an unresolvable condition is not a false one. A candidate value for the governing line changes none of this (SD-40).

O4.text: RATIFIED 6 October on Christian’s owner ruling, which supersedes the “dynamic object” framing of 5 October: “The Game Representation contains what a coach lays out and what the rules key on. It represents the rules governing game state, not the evolving state of the game itself. Accordingly: the ball belongs in the resolved representation when game rules key on it. Its live position does not, because that position is game state rather than game structure.” A layout position is therefore part of game STRUCTURE, and a ball’s live position is game STATE, so O4 is WITHDRAWN for a ball and its absence is not a gap. Where a restart does fix where the ball goes, that is a rule and belongs on T4 (transitions[].placement.region), which A01-02-07.a already uses. WHY THE NEGATIVE FORM: a positive list cannot obey this mechanism’s own rule, that an applicability condition may only ever remove a line it can positively disqualify. For a closed attribute like trigger a positive list satisfies that; for kind it does not, because the values are open-ended — two in live corpus selectors (zone, target) are absent from O2’s draft list, and an object selected kind=goalA was measured LOSING its authored layout position to a positive list. notIn disqualifies exactly the ball and keeps every other kind, including kinds nobody has named yet.
O4.sport: For soccer the ball is the immediate case. The rule is stated over structure versus state, not over football.

applicability.generalRule: Adopted 29 September on Christian ruling: a transition qualifier applies only where the transition trigger semantics make that qualifier structurally applicable. An inapplicable qualifier is WITHDRAWN; its absence is never a knowledge gap. Expressed as an applicability rule over the trigger, not as a special case for turnover - POSSESSION_CHANGE is named nowhere, it simply fails every out-of-play condition.
applicability.selectorGrammar: Added 29 September. An entry may condition on selectorAttribute instead of row. A selector attribute is fixed by stage 2 when the class is individuated, so the condition is decided at enumeration and the line is WITHDRAWN there rather than left CONDITIONAL on a governing line that can never move. Where the selector does not fix the attribute the condition is UNDECIDABLE and the line is KEPT, so an applicability rule can never hide a real gap.

teamDesignations.resolutionNote: ADDED 15 October 2026 (register version 9), for his M2 in the reply filed 17 October 2026: "M2 — Team-specific facts: Approved. Please implement the previously adopted September 20 designation rule, rather than introducing a narrower workaround solely for this activity. This is a reusable capability with applications beyond goalkeeper build-out." The adopted rule is AM-01 (derivation-spec-2026-09-20.md): "Use the game's transitions/episode context to resolve contextual team designations. An episode-scoped designation remains episode-scoped." Only that quoted sentence is his adopted text; the spec's elaboration beside it (a designation in a selector is met by each team the game's stated transitions make it at some trigger; the build-out team is the team awarded the start placement, KR-03; in a value designations compare as canonical entries) is the spec's. Each entry of the list now carries a TYPED RESOLUTION read by one resolver (back/src/system/derivation/designation.ts) for every consumer: what decides which team the designation picks out (kind) and for how long that answer holds (scope). basis GLOSS means the resolution restates the entry's own gloss above (or the ruling the gloss cites) and adds no meaning; basis OUR_INTERPRETATION means the entry has no gloss and the resolution is OUR reading under this list's note ("A designation is evaluated at the trigger or episode it is attached to"), shown to him and never quoted as his. The kinds and scopes are closed lists. A standing property of a team (a performer count, say) is reached only through a designation whose scope is in standingScopes: an EPISODE, DYNAMIC or TRIGGER designation never yields a standing value, because the team it picks out changes while the property does not. BLOCK_ROLE / BLOCK is registered for his M1 (role exchange by block) and no entry uses it yet; holding a role for a block is OUR extension of AM-01's 'episode-scoped remains episode-scoped' to a coach-called block, recorded outside his adopted text. Which instantiated team a SETUP_ASSIGNMENT designation picks out is a governed symmetric choice recorded by realization (SD-39, as the initial possession holder is), never derived from an ordinal.
teamDesignations.relativeToNote: ADDED 17 October 2026 (register version 14), for his reply filed 19 October 2026, item 1 ("Please ensure the underlying scoring eligibility reflects this distinction, rather than relying solely on the coach-facing wording.") and item 5 ("Any further changes should address general capabilities rather than introduce special cases for this Learning Goal."). A resolution may say, as data, how the team it picks out at a transition relates to the team a qualifier of that transition names (relativeTo: {qualifier, relation SAME | OTHER, words, citedAs}), so the one resolver (designation.ts awardeeRelation) can say whether a restart is awarded to a role's holder or away from it, with no designation named in code. OTHER is determinate only in a game holding exactly two teams.
